newsitem.title: JAPAN: Plutonium may have leaked from Japan nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: Plutonium may have leaked from Japan nuclear plant.

text.p: Radioactive particles collected after an explosion at Japan's nuclear reprocessing plant indicate that plutonium may have been released into the air, officials at the plant said on Saturday.
However, the level of radioactive particles found was below the limit set for areas outside the plant and did not pose any risk to the environment or to living beings, they said.

The state-run Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corporation (PNC) said high levels of alpha nuclide, or radioactive particles, were collected after Tuesday's explosion from filters attached to the plant ventilators.
Alpha nuclide is typically found in plutonium.

Minute amounts of plutonium in air and food enter the human body without causing major health problems, but when taken in large doses, the deadly poison can cause cancer and other serious illnesses, scientists say.

The explosion at the facility in Tokaimura, 160 km (100 miles) northeast of Tokyo, was caused by a fire that was not properly extinguished 10 hours earlier. The explosion allowed radiation to escape, exposing 37 workers to minor levels.
The PNC said late on Friday that the levels of alpha nuclide immediately after the explosion were ten times the normal level, higher than originally calculated.
However officials still saw no risk to living beings, and a a PNC spokesman stressed the new figures did not mean that plutonium was released into the air.
"Alpha nuclide is found typically in plutonium, but that does not mean plutonium was actually released in the air with that explosion," the spokesman told Reuters.
PNC said it will conduct experiments to determine if the particles were from plutonium from their facility or other elements such as polonium or uranium.
Test results were expected sometime early next week, the spokesman said.

The Tokaimura plant is Japan's only nuclear reprocessing facility, extracting plutonium from spent nuclear fuel. In 1994, plant operators sought international help when plutonium sludge collected inside the plant's reprocessing system.
The plant reprocesses about 12 percent of spent nuclear fuel from Japan's 50 running commercial nuclear power plants, with the rest reprocessed at French plants.
